# Approved 64-hex-character constants.
#
# The secret scan (.github/workflows/ci.yml and hooks/pre-commit) fails on any bare 64-hex string,
# because that is the shape of a private key and one committed by accident cannot be un-published.
#
# Matching on nearby keywords was tried first and is too weak in both directions: it misses constants
# whose name a formatter wrapped onto the previous line, and it would happily wave through a real key
# labelled `PUBKEY`. So the allowlist is by VALUE. Each entry is a constant a human has looked at and
# confirmed is safe to publish. Anything not listed here fails the build until someone adds it
# deliberately, with a reason.
#
# Do NOT add a value here to make a build pass. If you cannot write the justification, it does not
# belong in the repository.

# SHA-256 digests in the Metalink parser's test fixtures (crates/rdm-core/src/discover.rs). Published
# checksums of a public file, and an obviously-synthetic aabbcc… placeholder.
e907d92eeec9df64163a7e454cbc8d7755e8ddc7ed42f99dbc80c40f1a138433
aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899

# SHA-256 of silesia.zip, quoted in BENCHMARKS.md so the benchmark corpus can be verified as the
# canonical one rather than a re-upload. It is the digest of a file published at
# sun.aei.polsl.pl/~sdeor/corpus/silesia.zip and was confirmed identical on both benchmark machines.
0626e25f45c0ffb5dc801f13b7c82a3b75743ba07e3a71835a41e3d9f63c77af

# The two downloads the public benchmark corpus is built from, pinned in tools/corpus/make-corpus.py
# so a build that gets a different file stops instead of quietly producing a different corpus. Both
# are digests of publicly published files, downloaded and verified on the benchmark machine:
#   linux-6.12.tar.xz, matching the digest kernel.org publishes in its own sha256sums.asc
b1a2562be56e42afb3f8489d4c2a7ac472ac23098f1ef1c1e40da601f54625eb
#   bbb_sunflower_1080p_30fps_normal.mp4.zip from download.blender.org (Big Buck Bunny, CC BY 3.0)
e320fef389ec749117d0c1583945039266a40f25483881c2ff0d33207e62b362

# The identity of the benchmark corpus itself: a SHA-256 over its MANIFEST.sha256, quoted in
# tools/corpus/README.md so anyone who builds the corpus can confirm they got the same one. It is a
# digest of a list of digests and reveals nothing but the corpus contents, which are public by
# construction.
deb5f932d27a913ad6da2b994be7e66bffd03d6bf8546abd3de8ca7344efe599

# SHA-256 of cram-corpus-1.0.zip, the published download of that same corpus. Quoted next to the
# link in README.md, BENCHMARKS.md and tools/corpus/README.md so the download can be verified.
# The digest of a file we publish deliberately.
5be1b545ec9535834904a6436e6abf27a0fd607190851e314624e8a2db53faa7

# SHA-256 of licence files inside crates published on crates.io, pinned by the clarifications in
# about.toml so cargo-about picks the same licence text on every platform. Each is the digest of a
# public file, checked against the extracted crate on 2026-11-11:
#   libmimalloc-sys 0.1.49 LICENSE.txt
a08554fab028af3af047e8588d32d019662c1b1bf07959a195a2f75fe340726b
#   libmimalloc-sys 0.1.49 c_src/mimalloc/v2/LICENSE (v3/LICENSE is byte-identical)
82ade5d7d9b029044b5fbbc326207fc47c2d44ee4dd71e8a559c36d728217de9
#   miniz_oxide 0.8.9 LICENSE-MIT.md
799e9ca9d179295ef372f25d3769cdda7d25bb2668add6a6a1e22d1e4c678b8d
#   miniz_oxide 0.8.9 LICENSE-ZLIB.md
0a54e647fe54104658b5e563c04c6f9edf251710e47bce692e0bd990a4ddaa39
